nodes.name: Synchronized output regulation (SOR)
nodes.statement: As for the SOR, the requirements on output $y_i$ are two folds: one is that $y_i$ belongs to a fixed family of trajectories determined by the pair of $(s(w_0), q(w_0))$ with the corresponding initial condition $w_0(0)$ being allowed to vary on a predefined set $\hat{W}_0\subset W_0$; the other is that $y_i\rightarrow y_j$ for all $i,j\in\mathcal{V}$. The first one is the output regulation problem, which might be solved by a decentralized way and the second one is the synchronization problem, which has to rely on the information exchange to solve.
nodes.statement_short: SOR requires each agent output to lie in the trajectory family generated by $(s(w_0),q(w_0))$ and all outputs to agree.
differentia: $y_i$ belongs to a fixed family of trajectories determined by the pair of $(s(w_0), q(w_0))$
the other is that $y_i\rightarrow y_j$ for all $i,j\in\mathcal{V}$

nodes.name: Communication digraph
nodes.statement: Generally, a digraph $\mathcal{G}=\{\mathcal{V},\mathcal{E}\}$ is used to depict the communication channels of multi-agent system \eqref{II01}, where node set $\mathcal{V}=\{1,2,\cdots,N\}$ is the index set of agents and edge set $\mathcal{E}\subseteq \{\mathcal{V}\times \mathcal{V}\}$ consists of ordered pair of nodes $(i,j)$, called edge. An edge $(i,j)\in\mathcal{E}$ if and only if there is communication channel from node $i$ to node $j$, where node $i$ is called parent node and node $j$ is called child node.
nodes.statement_short: A digraph on the agent index set whose edges are directed communication channels, with parent/child terminology.
differentia: node set $\mathcal{V}=\{1,2,\cdots,N\}$ is the index set of agents
edge set $\mathcal{E}\subseteq \{\mathcal{V}\times \mathcal{V}\}$ consists of ordered pair of nodes $(i,j)$, called edge

nodes.name: Directed path
nodes.statement: A directed path of digraph is a sequence of edges with form $(i_1,i_2), (i_2,i_3), \cdots$.

nodes.name: Tree and root node
nodes.statement: A tree $\mathcal{G}_t=\{\mathcal{V}_t,\mathcal{E}_t\}$ is a graph where every node has exactly one parent node except for one node, the so-called root node, which has no parent node but has a directed path to every other node.
differentia: every node has exactly one parent node except for one node, the so-called root node, which has no parent node but has a directed path to every other node

nodes.name: Subgraph
nodes.statement: The graph $\mathcal{G}_s=\{\mathcal{V}_s,\mathcal{E}_s\}$ is a subgraph of $\mathcal{G}$ if $\mathcal{V}_s\subseteq\mathcal{V}$ and $\mathcal{E}_s\subseteq \mathcal{E}\bigcap(\mathcal{V}_s\times \mathcal{V}_s)$.

nodes.name: Spanning tree
nodes.statement: The tree $\mathcal{G}_t$ is a spanning tree of graph $\mathcal{G}$ if $\mathcal{G}_t$ is a subgraph of $\mathcal{G}$ with $\mathcal{V}_t=\mathcal{V}$.

nodes.name: Switching graph
nodes.statement: A switching graph, defined on a piecewise constant switching signal $\sigma(t):\real^+\mapsto \mathcal{P}=\{1,2,\cdots,P\}$, is denoted by $\mathcal{G}_{\sigma(t)}=\{\mathcal{V},\mathcal{E}_{\sigma(t)}\}$, where set $\mathcal{P}$ indexes the total $P$ number digraphs and $\mathcal{E}_{s}\subseteq\mathcal{V}\times \mathcal{V}$ with $s\in\mathcal{P}$. The time instants when $\sigma$ switches is denoted by an increasing sequence $t_k$, $k=0,1,2,\cdots,$ with $t_0=0$. Denote by $\sigma_k$ the value of $\sigma(t)$ when $t\in[t_{k-1},t_k)$. Denote by $\mathcal{A}^{\sigma_k}$ and $L^{\sigma_k}$ the adjacency matrix and the Laplacian matrix of $\mathcal{G}_{\sigma_k}$, respectively.
nodes.statement_short: A time-varying graph selected from $P$ digraphs by a piecewise-constant switching signal $\sigma(t)$, with switching instants $t_k$.
differentia: defined on a piecewise constant switching signal $\sigma(t):\real^+\mapsto \mathcal{P}=\{1,2,\cdots,P\}$
set $\mathcal{P}$ indexes the total $P$ number digraphs

nodes.name: Union graph
nodes.statement: A union graph $\mathcal{G}_{[t^1,t^2]}$ over an interval time $[t^1, t^2]$ is defined by $\mathcal{G}_{[t^1,t^2]}\triangleq (\mathcal{V}, \bigcup_{t\in[t^1,t^2]}\mathcal{E}_{\sigma(t)})$ that corresponds to a graph consisting of all nodes in $\mathcal{V}$ and all edges that appear at any time $t\in[t^1,t^2]$.
differentia: consisting of all nodes in $\mathcal{V}$ and all edges that appear at any time $t\in[t^1,t^2]$

nodes.name: Tracking error $e_i$
nodes.statement: In this case,  the tracking error for each agent is defined as \begin{equation} e_i = h_i(x_i)+q(w_i). \end{equation}

nodes.name: Maximum Lyapunov exponent $\nu_{max}$
nodes.statement: Denote by $\Phi_t^s(w^0)$ the flow of vector field $s(w_0)$, defined for all $t\in\real$,  with $w_0(0)=w^0$. Then the maximum Lyapunov exponent of dynamic system $\dot{w}_0=s(w_0)$ is defined as \cite{CenciniBOOK2010} \begin{equation} \nu_{max} = \lim_{t\rightarrow \infty} \lim_{\delta w^0\rightarrow 0}\frac{1}{t} \ln\frac{\|\Phi_t^s(w^0+\delta w^0)-\Phi_t^s(w^0)\|}{\|\delta w^0\|} \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Asymptotic exponential rate at which infinitesimally separated flows of $s$ diverge.

nodes.name: Consensus convergent rate $\alpha^*(T,t)$
nodes.statement: Given a switching graph $\mathcal{G}_{\sigma(t)}$ satisfying Assumption A4) with given $t$ and $T$, its consensus convergent rate is defined as the supremum of the contract rate of transition matrix $\Phi(t+(k-1)T,t+kT)$ \cite{XiangIJC2011}, \begin{equation} \alpha^*(T,t)=\sup_k \alpha(\Phi(t+(k-1)T,t+kT)) \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Worst-case contraction of the graph's transition matrix over successive windows of length $T$.
nodes.genus: the supremum of the contract rate of transition matrix $\Phi(t+(k-1)T,t+kT)$

nodes.name: Contract rate $\alpha(\Phi)$
nodes.statement: where the contract rate $\alpha(\Phi)$ is defined as $\alpha(\Phi) = \max\limits_{x\neq 0, x\bot \mathbf{b}}\frac{\|\Phi^Tx\|}{\|x\|}$
nodes.statement_short: Operator gain of $\Phi^T$ restricted to vectors orthogonal to the all-ones vector.

nodes.name: Transition matrix $\Phi(t^2,t^1)$
nodes.statement: the transition matrix is defined as \begin{equation} \Phi(t^2,t^1)=e^{-L^{\sigma_j}(t^2-t_{j-1})}e^{-L^{\sigma_{j-1}}\delta_{j-1}}\cdots e^{-L^{\sigma_{i+1}}\delta_{i+1}}e^{-L^{\sigma_{i}}(t_i-t^1)} \end{equation} where $L^{\sigma_k}$ is the Laplacian matrix of graph $\mathcal{G}_{\sigma_k}$. Throughout of this paper, $\mathbf{b}$ denotes the vector with all elements being $1$.
nodes.statement_short: Product of Laplacian matrix exponentials over the switching intervals between $t^1$ and $t^2$.

nodes.name: Remainder of the linear approximation $\psi_f$
nodes.statement: Denote by $\psi_{f}$ the reminder of the linear approximation of a vector function $f$, that is, \begin{equation} f(x)=f(0)+\left.\frac{\partial f}{\partial x}\right|_{x=0} x + \psi_f(x). \end{equation}
nodes.section: Solution of static feedback synchronized regulator problem

nodes.name: Jacobian matrix $\mathrm{D}f$
nodes.statement: Let $\mathrm{D}f$ denote the Jacobian matrix of vector function $f$, that is, $\mathrm{D}f(x) = \frac{\partial f}{\partial x}$. It follows that $\lim_{x\rightarrow 0}\psi_f(x)=0$ and $\lim_{x\rightarrow 0}\mathrm{D}\psi_f(x)=0$.
nodes.section: Solution of static feedback synchronized regulator problem

nodes.name: Averaged Jacobian operator $\mathrm{M}f(x,h)$
nodes.statement: Define \begin{equation} \mathrm{ M}f(x,h)=\left(\int^1_0 \mathrm{D}f(x+th)dt\right), \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Integral of the Jacobian of $f$ along the segment from $x$ to $x+h$.
nodes.section: Solution of static feedback synchronized regulator problem

nodes.name: Linearization matrices $A_i$, $B_i$, $C_i$
nodes.statement: Before proceeding the main results, some matrices are firstly introduced, arising from the linearization of nonlinear dynamics on the equilibrium of origin. \begin{equation} A_i = \left[ \frac{\partial f_i}{\partial x_i}\right]_{x_i=0},  \quad B_i = g_i(0), \quad \quad C_i= \left[ \frac{\partial h_i }{\partial x_i}\right]_{x_i=0}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Jacobian linearization $(A_i,B_i,C_i)$ of agent $i$'s dynamics at the origin.
nodes.section: Solution of static feedback synchronized regulator problem

nodes.name: Augmented graph $\bar{\mathcal{G}}$ with leader node
nodes.statement: Similar to that in \cite{WangTAC2010}, set the reference exosystem \begin{equation} \dot{w}_0=s(w_0) \end{equation} to be leader node, indexed as $0$, so as to form an augmented multi-agent system over an augmented graph $\bar{\mathcal{G}}=\{\bar{\mathcal{V}},\bar{\mathcal{E}}\}$, where $\bar{\mathcal{V}}=\{0\cup\mathcal{V}\}$ and $\bar{\mathcal{E}}=\{\mathcal{E}_0\cup\mathcal{E}\}$. Edge set $\mathcal{E}_0\subseteq \{0 \times \mathcal{V}\}$. $(0,i)\in\mathcal{E}_0$ if and only if node $i$ has the state information of reference exosystem $w_0$.
nodes.statement_short: Add the reference exosystem as node $0$ with edges to exactly those agents that receive $w_0$.
differentia: $(0,i)\in\mathcal{E}_0$ if and only if node $i$ has the state information of reference exosystem $w_0$

nodes.name: Leader-following output regulation
nodes.statement: While many real applications, such as power networks, require the output of each agent synchronizes on a designated reference trajectory. Such a case is referred to as leader-following output regulation and has been studied for linear systems, for example in \cite{XiangTAC2009} \cite{WangTAC2010} and \cite{SuTAC2012}.
differentia: require the output of each agent synchronizes on a designated reference trajectory

nodes.name: Dwell-time condition
nodes.statement: We assume that any two consecutive switching instants are separated by a dwell-time $D_t$, i.e., $t_k-t_{k-1}\ge D_t$ so as to guarantee that the switching graph is non-chattering and zeno behavior cannot occur.

nodes.name: Assumption A1) — Poisson stable exosystem
nodes.statement: The exosystem modeled by $\dot{w}_0=s(w_0)$ has a stable equilibrium at $w_0=0$, and there is an open neighborhood of $w_0=0$ in which every point is Poisson stable.

nodes.name: Assumption A2) — stabilizable linear approximation
nodes.statement: The pair $\big(f_i(x_i),g_i(x_i)\big)$ has a stabilizable linear approximation at $x_i=0$, for all $i\in\mathcal{V}$.

nodes.name: Assumption A3) — detectable linear approximation
nodes.statement: The pair $\big(f_i(x_i),h_i(x_i)\big)$ has a detectable linear approximation at $x_i=0$ for all $i\in\mathcal{V}$.

nodes.name: Assumption A4) — bounded interconnectivity times condition
nodes.statement: There is a bounded time length $T$ and a starting time $t>0$ such that for each $k$, $k=1,2,\cdots$, the union graph $\mathcal{G}_{[t+(k-1)T,t+kT]}$ has a spanning tree embedded.
nodes.statement_short: Over every window of length $T$ the union of the switching graphs contains a spanning tree.

nodes.name: Assumption A5) — bounded interconnectivity times on the augmented graph
nodes.statement: There is a bounded time length $T$ and a starting time $t>0$ such that for each $k$, $k=1,2,\cdots$, the union graph $\bar{\mathcal{G}}_{[t+(k-1)T,t+kT]}$ has a spanning tree embedded.
nodes.statement_short: Assumption A4) restated on the leader-augmented graph $\bar{\mathcal{G}}$.

nodes.name: Agent dynamics
nodes.statement: Consider a multi-agent system consisting of $N$ agents. Each agent has the following dynamics modeled by \begin{equation} \left\{\begin{split} \dot{x}_i &= f_i(x_i)+g_i(x_i)u_i  \\ y_i & = h_i(x_i), \end{split}\right., \quad  i=1,2,\cdots,N, \end{equation} where $x_i$ is the state, defined on a neighborhood $X_i$ of the origin of $\real^{n_i}$, $u_i\in\real^{m_i}$ is the input, and $y_i\in\real^p$ is the output. The vector $f_i(x_i)$ and the $m_i$ columns of matrix $g_i(x_i)$ are smooth (i.e., $C^{\infty}$) vector fields on $X_i$. $h_i(x_i)$ is a smooth mapping defined on $X_i$.
nodes.statement_short: Each of the $N$ agents is a smooth nonlinear input-affine system with output $y_i=h_i(x_i)$.

nodes.name: Common exosystem and output tracking requirement
nodes.statement: Each agent drives its output to track the output of a common exosystem, as formulated by \begin{subequations} \begin{align} &\dot{w}_0=s(w_0)\\ &y_i+q(w_0)\rightarrow 0. \end{align} \end{subequations} The first equation describes an autonomous system, the so-called exosystem, defined in a neighborhood $W_0$ of the origin of $\real^s$. The second equation means that the output should track a reference signal produced by the exosystem. The vector $s(w_0)$ is a smooth vector field on $W_0$ and $q(w_0)$ is a smooth map defined on $W_0$.
nodes.statement_short: An autonomous exosystem $\dot{w}_0=s(w_0)$ generates the reference $-q(w_0)$ that every output must track.

nodes.name: Coupled exosystem
nodes.statement: In the first step, each agent builds the following coupled exosystem, based on the communication graph $\mathcal{G}_{\sigma(t)}$, \begin{equation} \dot{w}_i = s(w_i)+\sum_{j=1}^N a_{ij}^{\sigma(t)}(w_j-w_i), \end{equation} where $a_{ij}^{\sigma(t)}$ denotes the $i$th row and $j$th column element of adjacency matrix $\mathcal{A}^{\sigma(t)}$ of graph $\mathcal{G}_{\sigma(t)}$. If $(j,i)\in\mathcal{E}_{\sigma(t)}$, then $a^{\sigma(t)}_{ij}>0$; otherwise, $a^{\sigma(t)}_{ij}=0$.
nodes.statement_short: Each agent runs a local copy of the exosystem with diffusive coupling over the switching graph.

nodes.name: Distributed dynamic state feedback controller
nodes.statement: \textbf{Distributed dynamic state feedback controller} \begin{equation} \left\{ \begin{split} & \dot{w}_i = s(w_i)+\sum_{j=1}^N a_{ij}^{\sigma(t)}(w_j-w_i),\\ & u_i = \alpha_i(x_i,w_i) \end{split} \right.,  \quad i\in\mathcal{V}, \end{equation} where $\alpha_i(x_i,w_i)$ is a $C^k$ (for some integer $k\ge2$) mapping defined on $X_i\times W$, satisfying $a_i(0,0)=0$.
nodes.statement_short: Local exosystem plus a static map of the agent state and local exosystem state as input.

nodes.name: Closed-loop system under state feedback
nodes.statement: Combining \eqref{II04} and \eqref{II01} yields the following closed-loop system, \begin{equation} \left\{\begin{split} \dot{x}_i& = f_i(x_i)+g_i(x_i)\alpha_i(x_i,w_i)  \\ \dot{w}_i& = s(w_i)+\sum_{j=1}^N a_{ij}^{\sigma(t)}(w_j-w_i) \end{split}, \right.\quad i\in\mathcal{V}, \end{equation} which has an equilibrium at, $(x_i,w_i)=(0,0)$ for all $i\in\mathcal{V}$.

nodes.name: Distributed dynamic output feedback controller
nodes.statement: \textbf{Distributed dynamic output feedback controller} \begin{equation} \left\{ \begin{split} \dot{w}_i& = s(w_i)+\sum_{j=1}^N a_{ij}^{\sigma(t)}(w_j-w_i)\\ \dot{z}_i& = \eta_i(z_i,y_i)\\ u_i &= \alpha_i(z_i,w_i) \end{split}, \right. \quad i\in\mathcal{V}, \end{equation} where $z_i\in\real^{n_i}$ is the observer state, defined on a neighborhood $Z_i$ of the origin of $\real^{n_i}$.  For each $y_i\in\real^p$, $\eta_i(z_i,y_i)$ is a $C^k$ vector field on $Z_i$ (for some integer $k\ge 2$).
nodes.statement_short: Local exosystem plus an observer driven by $y_i$, with input a static map of observer and exosystem states.

nodes.name: Closed-loop system under output feedback
nodes.statement: The closed-loop system under controller \eqref{II06} has the form \begin{equation} \left\{ \begin{split} \dot{x}_i&=f_i(x_i)+g_i(x_i)\alpha_i(z_i,w_i)\\ \dot{z}_i &  = \eta_i(z_i,h_i(x_i))\\ \dot{w}_i & = s(w_i) + \sum_{j=1}^N a_{ij}^{\sigma(t)}(w_j-w_i) \end{split}, \right.\quad i\in\mathcal{V}, \end{equation} which has an equilibrium, $(x_i,z_i,w_i)=(0,0,0)$ for all $i\in\mathcal{V}$, when $\eta_i(0,0)=0$ for all $i\in\mathcal{V}$.

nodes.name: Regulator equation
nodes.statement: \begin{subequations} \begin{align} &\frac{\partial \pi_i}{\partial w_0} s(w_0) = f_i(\pi_i(w_0))+g_i(\pi_i(w_0))c_i(w_0) \\ &h_i(\pi_i(w_0))+q(w_0)=0 \end{align} \end{subequations}
nodes.statement_short: Regulator equation: an invariant manifold condition plus exact output-zeroing for agent $i$.
nodes.section: Solution of static feedback synchronized regulator problem

nodes.name: Leader-following coupled exosystem
nodes.statement: In such a configuration, the first equation in controllers both \eqref{II04} and \eqref{II06} should be changed to be \begin{equation} \dot{w}_i=s(w_i)+\sum_{j=0}^N \bar{a}_{ij}^{\sigma(t)}(w_j-w_i), \quad i\in\mathcal{V}, \end{equation} where $\bar{a}^{\sigma(t)}_{ij}$ denotes the element of adjacency matrix $\bar{A}^{\sigma(t)}$ of diagraph $\bar{\mathcal{G}}_{\sigma(t)}$.
nodes.statement_short: Coupled exosystem summed from $j=0$ so that the leader state $w_0$ enters the coupling.

nodes.name: Mean-value expansion of the linear-approximation remainder
nodes.statement: then by mean-value theorem, \begin{equation} \psi_f(x+h)=\psi_f(x)+\mathrm{M}\psi_f(x,h)h. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: The remainder increment factors exactly through the averaged Jacobian $\mathrm{M}\psi_f(x,h)$.
nodes.section: Solution of static feedback synchronized regulator problem

nodes.name: State Feedback Synchronized Regulator Problem
nodes.statement: [\textbf{State Feedback Synchronized Regulator Problem}] Find, if possible, $\alpha_i(x_i,w_i)$ for node $i$ such that: \begin{enumerate} \item [1a)] the equilibrium $x=0$ of \begin{equation} \dot{x}_i = f_i(x_i)+g_i(x_i)\alpha_i(x_i,0), \quad i\in\mathcal{V} \end{equation} is exponentially stable. \item [1b)] there are a neighborhood $U\subset X\times W$ of $(0,0)$ and a exosystem, \begin{equation} \dot{w}_0=s(w_0), \end{equation} defined on the neighborhood $W_0$ of origin of $\real^{s}$, such that, for each initial condition $(x(0),w(0))\in U$, there exists a initial condition $w_0(0)\in W_0$ for system \eqref{II09} such that the solution of \eqref{II05} satisfies \begin{equation} \lim_{t\rightarrow \infty} (h_i(x_i(t))+q(w_0(t))) = 0, \quad \forall\, i\in\mathcal{V}. \end{equation} \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Design $\alpha_i(x_i,w_i)$ making the unforced equilibrium exponentially stable and driving all tracking errors to zero.

nodes.name: Error feedback Synchronized Regulator Problem
nodes.statement: [\textbf{Error feedback Synchronized Regulator Problem}] Find, if possible, $\alpha_i(z_i,w_i)$ and $\eta_i(z_i,y_i)$, such that \begin{itemize} \item [2a)] the equilibrium $(x,z)=0$ of \begin{equation} \begin{split} &\dot{x}_i=f_i(x_i)+g_i(x_i)\alpha_i(z_i,0),\\ & \dot{z}_i=\eta_i(z_i,h_i(x_i)), \end{split}\quad \quad i\in\mathcal{V}, \end{equation} is exponentially stable. \item [2b)] there exists a neighborhood $U\subset X\times Z\times W$ of $(0,0,0)$ and an exosystem \begin{equation} \dot{w}_0=s(w_0) \end{equation} defined on a neighborhood $W_0$ of origin of $\real^{s}$, such that, for each initial condition $(x(0), z(0)$, $ w(0))\in U$, there exists a initial condition $w_0(0)\in W_0$ for system \eqref{II12} such that the solution of \eqref{II07} satisfies \begin{equation} \lim_{t\rightarrow \infty} (h_i(x_i(t))+q(w_0(t)))=0, \quad \forall\, i\in\mathcal{V}. \end{equation} \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: Design $\alpha_i(z_i,w_i)$ and observer dynamics $\eta_i(z_i,y_i)$ achieving exponential stability and asymptotic output tracking.

nodes.name: Lemma 1 (local exponential synchronizability of coupled exosystems)
nodes.statement: Given a multi-agent system \eqref{II02} with communication graph $\mathcal{G}_{\sigma(t)}$satisfying assumption A4). If the largest Lyapunov exponent $\nu_{max}$ of system $\dot{w}_0=s(w_0)$ and the consensus convergence rate $\alpha^*(T,t)$ of $\mathcal{G}_{\sigma(t)}$ are such that \begin{equation} \nu_{max}+\ln(\alpha^*(T,t))/T<0 \end{equation} then system \eqref{II02} is locally exponentially synchronizable.
nodes.statement_short: If graph contraction beats the exosystem's expansion rate, the coupled exosystems synchronize exponentially.

This is contradictory to the feature of Poisson stable \cite{IsidoriTAC1990}. With $\nu_{max}\le0$ and $\alpha^*(T,t)<1$, making use of Lemma \ref{le01} yields that there is a neighborhood $\bar{W}\subset W$ of origin, for all initial condition $w(0)\in\bar{W}$, all the exosystems have their states exponentially synchronize on a manifold determined by $\dot{w}_0=s(w_0)$ with $w_0\in\mathcal{W}^0$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3
nodes.statement: According to Assumption A2), it is true that there exists a matrix $K_i$ such that $A_i+B_iK_i$ is Hurwitz for all $i\in\mathcal{V}$. Noting that $\alpha_i(x_i,0)=K_ix_i$, condition 1a) follows directly. Below we show condition 1b). By Lemma \ref{le02}, there is a positive scalar $\beta_1$ such that \begin{equation} \|\delta w_i(t)\| \le \epsilon_0 e^{-\beta_1t}\|\delta w_i(0)\|, \quad \forall\,\, i\in\mathcal{V}, \end{equation} for some positive scalar $\epsilon_0$. Consider the vector $e_{xi}=x_i-\pi_i(w_0)$. With \eqref{III09a}, its dynamics has the form \begin{equation} \dot{e}_{xi}=f_i(x_i)+g_i(x_i)\alpha_i(x_i,w_i)-f_i(\pi_i(w_0))-g_i(\pi_i(w_0))c_i(w_0). \end{equation} Making use of linear approximation and mean value theorem, one has, \begin{equation} f_i(x_i)-f_i(\pi_i(w_0))=A_ie_{xi}+\psi_{f_i}(x_i)-\psi_{f_i}(\pi_i(w_0)) = A_ie_{xi}+\mathrm{M}\psi_{f_i}(\pi_i(w_0),e_{x_i})e_{x_i} \end{equation} and \begin{equation} \begin{split} g_i(x_i)&\alpha_i(x_i,w_i)-g_i(\pi_i(w_0))c_i(w_0) = g_i(x_i)c_i(w_i)-g_i(\pi_i(w_0))c_i(w_0)+g_i(x_i)K_ie_{xi}\\ =&(g_i(x_i)-g_i(\pi_i(w_0)))c_i(w_0)+g_i(x_i)(\mathrm{M}c_i(w_0,\delta{w_i})\delta{w_i}+K_ie_{xi})\\ =&B_iK_ie_{xi}+ \left[\mathrm{M}g_{ij}(0,x_i)x_i,\cdots, \mathrm{M}g_{im_i}(0,x_i)x_i\right]K_ie_{xi}+ g_i(x_i)\mathrm{M}c_i(w_0,\delta{w_i})\delta{w_i} \\& +\left(\sum_{j=1}^{m_i} c_{ij}(w_0)\mathrm{M}g_{ij}(\pi_i(w_0),e_{xi})\right)e_{xi} \end{split} \end{equation} where $g_{ij}(x_i)$ denotes the $j$th column vector of matrix function $g_i(x_i)$ and $c_{ij}(w_0)$ denotes the $j$th element of $c_i(w_0)$. With the above two equations, equation \eqref{III12} can be rewritten as \begin{equation} \dot{e}_{xi}=(A_i+B_iK_i)e_{xi}+ N(w_0,x_i)e_{xi}+g_i(x_i)\mathrm{M}c_i(w_0,\delta w_i)\delta w_i, \quad i\in\mathcal{V}, \end{equation} where \begin{equation} \begin{split} N(w_0,x_i)&=\mathrm{M}\psi_{f_i}(\pi_i(w_0),x_i-\pi_i(w_0))+\sum_{j=1}^{m_i} c_{ij}(w_0)\mathrm{M}g_{ij}(\pi_i(w_0),x_i-\pi_i(w_0)) \\&+ \left[\mathrm{M}g_{ij}(0,x_i)x_i,\cdots, \mathrm{M}g_{im_i}(0,x_i)x_i\right]K_i \end{split}. \end{equation} Since $A_i+B_iK_i$ is Hurwitz, there are a symmetric positive definite matrix $P_i\in\real^{n_i\times n_i}$ and a positive scalara $\epsilon_1$ such that \begin{equation} P_i(A_i+B_iK_i)+(A_i+B_iK_i)^TP_i+2\epsilon_1P_i<-I_{n_i}. \end{equation} By assumption A1) and noticing that condition 1a) holds, there exist sufficiently small $w_i(0)$ and $x_i(0)$ (notice that $w_0$ depends on $w_i$, $i\in\mathcal{V}$), such that the trajectories of $x_i(t)$ and $w_i(t)$ of the closed-loop system \eqref{II05} satisfy \begin{equation} \|N(w_0(t),x_i(t))\|\le \frac{1}{2\lambda_M(P_i)},\,\, \,\, \|g_i(x_i(t))\mathrm{M}c_i(w_0(t),\delta w_i(t))\|\le \frac{1}{\lambda_M(P_i)}, \quad \forall t>0. \end{equation} where $\lambda_M(P_i)$ denotes the maximum eigenvalue of $P_i$. Then consider the Lyapunov function $V_i=e_{xi}^TP_ie_{xi}$, whose derivative satisfies \begin{equation} \dot{V}_i\le - 2\epsilon_1e_{xi}^TP_ie_{xi} + 2e_{xi}^TP_i g_i(x_i)\mathrm{M}c_i(w_0,\delta w_i)\delta w_i \le -2\epsilon_1 V_i + 2\epsilon_2 \sqrt{V_i}\|\delta w_i\|, \end{equation} where $\epsilon_2>\frac{1}{\sqrt{\lambda_{m}(P_i)}}$ is a constant scalar and $\lambda_m(P_i)$ denoting the minimal eigenvalue of $P_i$. Define $\bar{V}_i=\sqrt{V}_i$, then $\bar{V}_i\ge0$ and \begin{equation} \dot{\bar{V}}_i\le -\epsilon_1\bar{V}_i+\epsilon_2 \|\delta w_i\|, \end{equation} which is equivalent to $\left(e^{\epsilon_1t}\bar{V}_i\right)'\le \epsilon_2 e^{\epsilon_1t}\|\delta w_i\|$. With \eqref{III11}, one further obtains \begin{equation} \bar{V}_i(t)\le  e^{-\epsilon_1 t}\left(\bar{V}_i(0)-\frac{\epsilon_2\epsilon_0\|\delta w_i(0)\|}{\epsilon_1-\beta_1} \right) + e^{-\beta_1 t}\frac{\epsilon_2\epsilon_0\|\delta w_i(0)\|}{\epsilon_1-\beta_1}, \end{equation} from which, $\bar{V}_i(t)\rightarrow 0$ as $t\rightarrow \infty$, and so does $e_{xi}$. Using \eqref{III09b}, it can be further concluded that condition 1b) will be satisfied.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2
nodes.statement: Necessity is clear. Below we show the sufficiency by using a constructive method. Assumption A2) and A3) mean that there are matrices $K_i$ and $L_i$ such that \setcounter{equation}{21} \begin{equation} A_i+B_iK_i \quad \mbox{and}\quad A_i+L_iC_i \end{equation} are Hurwitz. By them, the following matrix \begin{equation} \begin{bmatrix} A_i & B_iK_i \\ -L_iC_i & A_i+B_iK_i+L_iC_i \end{bmatrix} \end{equation} is also Hurwitz. Suppose there are two maps $\pi_i(w_0)$ and $c_i(w_0)$ satisfying \eqref{III09}, then set the dynamic controller to be \begin{subequations} \begin{align} &u_i=\alpha_i(z_i,w_i)=c_i(w_i)+K_i(z_i-\pi_i(w_i)), \\ &\dot{z}_{i}=\eta_i(z_i,h_i)=f_i(z_{i})+g_i(z_{i})u_i+L_i(h_i(z_i)-h_i(x_i)), \end{align} \end{subequations} for all $i\in\mathcal{V}$. Define the augmented state $\tilde{x}_i = [x_i^T, z_i^T]^T$, and maps \begin{gather} \tilde{f}_i({\tilde{x}_i})=\begin{bmatrix} f_i(x_i)\\ -L_ih_i(x_i)+L_ih_i(z_i)+f_i(z_i) \end{bmatrix}, \quad \tilde{g}_i(\tilde{x}_i)=\begin{bmatrix} g_i(x_i) \\ g_i(z_i) \end{bmatrix}, \nonumber \\ \tilde{\pi}_i(w_0)=\begin{bmatrix} \pi_i(w_0) \\ \pi_i(w_0) \end{bmatrix}, \quad \tilde{h}_i(\tilde{x}_i)=h_i(x_i). \end{gather} With them, one has \begin{equation} \dot{\tilde{x}}_i = \tilde{f}_i(\tilde{x}_i)+\tilde{g}_i(\tilde{x}_i)u_i, \quad \tilde{y}_i=\tilde{h}_i(\tilde{x}_i), \quad i\in\mathcal{V}, \end{equation} and \begin{equation} \begin{split} &\frac{\partial \tilde{\pi}_i}{\partial w_0} s(w_0) = \tilde{f}_i(\tilde{\pi}_i(w_0))+\tilde{g}_i(\tilde{\pi}_i(w_0))c_i(w_0), \\ &\tilde{h}_i(\tilde{\pi}_i(w_0))+q(w_0)=0. \end{split} \end{equation} The Jacobian matrices of $\tilde{f}_i(\tilde{x}_i)$ and $\tilde{g}_i(\tilde{x}_i)$ have the form of \begin{equation} \tilde{A}_i=\left[ \frac{\partial \tilde{f}_i}{\partial \tilde{x}_i} \right]_{\tilde{x}_i=0}=\begin{bmatrix} A_i & 0 \\ -L_iC_i & A_i+L_iC_i \end{bmatrix}, \quad \tilde{B}_i=\left[ \frac{\partial \tilde{g}_i}{\partial \tilde{x}_i} \right]_{\tilde{x}_i=0}=\begin{bmatrix} B_i & 0 \\ 0 & B_i \end{bmatrix} \end{equation} Noting that $\tilde{A}_i+\tilde{B}_i[0, K_i]$ has exactly the form \eqref{III23} and that controller \eqref{III24a} can be rewritten as $u_i=c_i(w_i)+[0, K_i](\tilde{x}_i-\tilde{\pi}_i(w_i))$, by Lemma \ref{le03} conditions 1a) and 1b) are satisfied for multi-agent system \eqref{III26} with controller \eqref{III24a}, and subsequently conditions 2a) and 2b) are satisfied for the closed-loop system \eqref{II07}. Therefore the output feedback synchronized regulator problem is solved under controller \eqref{III24}.

nodes.name: Condition 1a) via a Hurwitz gain
nodes.statement: According to Assumption A2), it is true that there exists a matrix $K_i$ such that $A_i+B_iK_i$ is Hurwitz for all $i\in\mathcal{V}$. Noting that $\alpha_i(x_i,0)=K_ix_i$, condition 1a) follows directly. Below we show condition 1b).
nodes.statement_short: Use A2) to pick a stabilizing $K_i$, which settles condition 1a).
nodes.section: Solution of static feedback synchronized regulator problem

nodes.name: Exponential bound on the exosystem error
nodes.statement: By Lemma \ref{le02}, there is a positive scalar $\beta_1$ such that \begin{equation} \|\delta w_i(t)\| \le \epsilon_0 e^{-\beta_1t}\|\delta w_i(0)\|, \quad \forall\,\, i\in\mathcal{V}, \end{equation} for some positive scalar $\epsilon_0$.
nodes.statement_short: Invoke Lemma 2 for an exponentially decaying bound on $\|\delta w_i(t)\|$.
nodes.section: Solution of static feedback synchronized regulator problem

nodes.name: Introduce the manifold error $e_{xi}$
nodes.statement: Consider the vector $e_{xi}=x_i-\pi_i(w_0)$. With \eqref{III09a}, its dynamics has the form \begin{equation} \dot{e}_{xi}=f_i(x_i)+g_i(x_i)\alpha_i(x_i,w_i)-f_i(\pi_i(w_0))-g_i(\pi_i(w_0))c_i(w_0). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Define the deviation from the invariant manifold and write its dynamics.
nodes.section: Solution of static feedback synchronized regulator problem

nodes.name: Expand the drift and input terms by the mean value theorem
nodes.statement: Making use of linear approximation and mean value theorem, one has, \begin{equation} f_i(x_i)-f_i(\pi_i(w_0))=A_ie_{xi}+\psi_{f_i}(x_i)-\psi_{f_i}(\pi_i(w_0)) = A_ie_{xi}+\mathrm{M}\psi_{f_i}(\pi_i(w_0),e_{x_i})e_{x_i} \end{equation} and \begin{equation} \begin{split} g_i(x_i)&\alpha_i(x_i,w_i)-g_i(\pi_i(w_0))c_i(w_0) = g_i(x_i)c_i(w_i)-g_i(\pi_i(w_0))c_i(w_0)+g_i(x_i)K_ie_{xi}\\ =&(g_i(x_i)-g_i(\pi_i(w_0)))c_i(w_0)+g_i(x_i)(\mathrm{M}c_i(w_0,\delta{w_i})\delta{w_i}+K_ie_{xi})\\ =&B_iK_ie_{xi}+ \left[\mathrm{M}g_{ij}(0,x_i)x_i,\cdots, \mathrm{M}g_{im_i}(0,x_i)x_i\right]K_ie_{xi}+ g_i(x_i)\mathrm{M}c_i(w_0,\delta{w_i})\delta{w_i} \\& +\left(\sum_{j=1}^{m_i} c_{ij}(w_0)\mathrm{M}g_{ij}(\pi_i(w_0),e_{xi})\right)e_{xi} \end{split} \end{equation} where $g_{ij}(x_i)$ denotes the $j$th column vector of matrix function $g_i(x_i)$ and $c_{ij}(w_0)$ denotes the $j$th element of $c_i(w_0)$.
nodes.statement_short: Split both differences into linear parts plus averaged-Jacobian remainders.
nodes.section: Solution of static feedback synchronized regulator problem

nodes.name: Rewrite the error dynamics with perturbation $N(w_0,x_i)$
nodes.statement: With the above two equations, equation \eqref{III12} can be rewritten as \begin{equation} \dot{e}_{xi}=(A_i+B_iK_i)e_{xi}+ N(w_0,x_i)e_{xi}+g_i(x_i)\mathrm{M}c_i(w_0,\delta w_i)\delta w_i, \quad i\in\mathcal{V}, \end{equation} where \begin{equation} \begin{split} N(w_0,x_i)&=\mathrm{M}\psi_{f_i}(\pi_i(w_0),x_i-\pi_i(w_0))+\sum_{j=1}^{m_i} c_{ij}(w_0)\mathrm{M}g_{ij}(\pi_i(w_0),x_i-\pi_i(w_0)) \\&+ \left[\mathrm{M}g_{ij}(0,x_i)x_i,\cdots, \mathrm{M}g_{im_i}(0,x_i)x_i\right]K_i \end{split}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Recast the error dynamics as a Hurwitz linear part plus a vanishing perturbation and a $\delta w_i$ input.
nodes.section: Solution of static feedback synchronized regulator problem

nodes.name: Lyapunov matrix from the Hurwitz property
nodes.statement: Since $A_i+B_iK_i$ is Hurwitz, there are a symmetric positive definite matrix $P_i\in\real^{n_i\times n_i}$ and a positive scalara $\epsilon_1$ such that \begin{equation} P_i(A_i+B_iK_i)+(A_i+B_iK_i)^TP_i+2\epsilon_1P_i<-I_{n_i}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Obtain $P_i>0$ solving a strict Lyapunov inequality with margin $\epsilon_1$.
nodes.section: Solution of static feedback synchronized regulator problem

nodes.name: Smallness bounds on the perturbation terms
nodes.statement: By assumption A1) and noticing that condition 1a) holds, there exist sufficiently small $w_i(0)$ and $x_i(0)$ (notice that $w_0$ depends on $w_i$, $i\in\mathcal{V}$), such that the trajectories of $x_i(t)$ and $w_i(t)$ of the closed-loop system \eqref{II05} satisfy \begin{equation} \|N(w_0(t),x_i(t))\|\le \frac{1}{2\lambda_M(P_i)},\,\, \,\, \|g_i(x_i(t))\mathrm{M}c_i(w_0(t),\delta w_i(t))\|\le \frac{1}{\lambda_M(P_i)}, \quad \forall t>0. \end{equation} where $\lambda_M(P_i)$ denotes the maximum eigenvalue of $P_i$.
nodes.statement_short: For small initial conditions the perturbation and input gains stay below $1/\lambda_M(P_i)$-type bounds.
nodes.section: Solution of static feedback synchronized regulator problem

nodes.name: Lyapunov function derivative estimate
nodes.statement: Then consider the Lyapunov function $V_i=e_{xi}^TP_ie_{xi}$, whose derivative satisfies \begin{equation} \dot{V}_i\le - 2\epsilon_1e_{xi}^TP_ie_{xi} + 2e_{xi}^TP_i g_i(x_i)\mathrm{M}c_i(w_0,\delta w_i)\delta w_i \le -2\epsilon_1 V_i + 2\epsilon_2 \sqrt{V_i}\|\delta w_i\|, \end{equation} where $\epsilon_2>\frac{1}{\sqrt{\lambda_{m}(P_i)}}$ is a constant scalar and $\lambda_m(P_i)$ denoting the minimal eigenvalue of $P_i$.
nodes.statement_short: Bound $\dot{V}_i$ by $-2\epsilon_1V_i+2\epsilon_2\sqrt{V_i}\|\delta w_i\|$.
nodes.section: Solution of static feedback synchronized regulator problem

nodes.name: Comparison argument and conclusion of condition 1b)
nodes.statement: Define $\bar{V}_i=\sqrt{V}_i$, then $\bar{V}_i\ge0$ and \begin{equation} \dot{\bar{V}}_i\le -\epsilon_1\bar{V}_i+\epsilon_2 \|\delta w_i\|, \end{equation} which is equivalent to $\left(e^{\epsilon_1t}\bar{V}_i\right)'\le \epsilon_2 e^{\epsilon_1t}\|\delta w_i\|$. With \eqref{III11}, one further obtains \begin{equation} \bar{V}_i(t)\le  e^{-\epsilon_1 t}\left(\bar{V}_i(0)-\frac{\epsilon_2\epsilon_0\|\delta w_i(0)\|}{\epsilon_1-\beta_1} \right) + e^{-\beta_1 t}\frac{\epsilon_2\epsilon_0\|\delta w_i(0)\|}{\epsilon_1-\beta_1}, \end{equation} from which, $\bar{V}_i(t)\rightarrow 0$ as $t\rightarrow \infty$, and so does $e_{xi}$. Using \eqref{III09b}, it can be further concluded that condition 1b) will be satisfied.
nodes.statement_short: Integrate the comparison inequality to get $e_{xi}\to0$, then use the output-zeroing condition to conclude 1b).
nodes.section: Solution of static feedback synchronized regulator problem

nodes.name: Necessity via the single-agent case
nodes.statement: Necessity is obvious by considering the special situation with $N=1$.
nodes.statement_short: Specialize to $N=1$ to inherit the classical necessity.
nodes.section: Solution of static feedback synchronized regulator problem

nodes.name: Sufficiency from Lemma 3
nodes.statement: The sufficiency follows immediately from Lemma \ref{le03}.
nodes.statement_short: Apply Lemma 3 for sufficiency.
nodes.section: Solution of static feedback synchronized regulator problem

nodes.name: Necessity
nodes.statement: Necessity is clear.
nodes.statement_short: Necessity asserted without further argument.
nodes.section: Solution of output feedback synchronized regulator problem

nodes.name: Hurwitz gain and observer matrices
nodes.statement: Below we show the sufficiency by using a constructive method. Assumption A2) and A3) mean that there are matrices $K_i$ and $L_i$ such that \setcounter{equation}{21} \begin{equation} A_i+B_iK_i \quad \mbox{and}\quad A_i+L_iC_i \end{equation} are Hurwitz. By them, the following matrix \begin{equation} \begin{bmatrix} A_i & B_iK_i \\ -L_iC_i & A_i+B_iK_i+L_iC_i \end{bmatrix} \end{equation} is also Hurwitz.
nodes.statement_short: Use A2) and A3) to get stabilizing and observer gains whose composite matrix is Hurwitz.
nodes.section: Solution of output feedback synchronized regulator problem

nodes.name: Construct the dynamic controller
nodes.statement: Suppose there are two maps $\pi_i(w_0)$ and $c_i(w_0)$ satisfying \eqref{III09}, then set the dynamic controller to be \begin{subequations} \begin{align} &u_i=\alpha_i(z_i,w_i)=c_i(w_i)+K_i(z_i-\pi_i(w_i)), \\ &\dot{z}_{i}=\eta_i(z_i,h_i)=f_i(z_{i})+g_i(z_{i})u_i+L_i(h_i(z_i)-h_i(x_i)), \end{align} \end{subequations} for all $i\in\mathcal{V}$.
nodes.statement_short: Build an observer-based controller from the regulator-equation solutions.
nodes.section: Solution of output feedback synchronized regulator problem

nodes.name: Augmented state and augmented regulator equation
nodes.statement: Define the augmented state $\tilde{x}_i = [x_i^T, z_i^T]^T$, and maps \begin{gather} \tilde{f}_i({\tilde{x}_i})=\begin{bmatrix} f_i(x_i)\\ -L_ih_i(x_i)+L_ih_i(z_i)+f_i(z_i) \end{bmatrix}, \quad \tilde{g}_i(\tilde{x}_i)=\begin{bmatrix} g_i(x_i) \\ g_i(z_i) \end{bmatrix}, \nonumber \\ \tilde{\pi}_i(w_0)=\begin{bmatrix} \pi_i(w_0) \\ \pi_i(w_0) \end{bmatrix}, \quad \tilde{h}_i(\tilde{x}_i)=h_i(x_i). \end{gather} With them, one has \begin{equation} \dot{\tilde{x}}_i = \tilde{f}_i(\tilde{x}_i)+\tilde{g}_i(\tilde{x}_i)u_i, \quad \tilde{y}_i=\tilde{h}_i(\tilde{x}_i), \quad i\in\mathcal{V}, \end{equation} and \begin{equation} \begin{split} &\frac{\partial \tilde{\pi}_i}{\partial w_0} s(w_0) = \tilde{f}_i(\tilde{\pi}_i(w_0))+\tilde{g}_i(\tilde{\pi}_i(w_0))c_i(w_0), \\ &\tilde{h}_i(\tilde{\pi}_i(w_0))+q(w_0)=0. \end{split} \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Stack plant and observer into one system for which the regulator equation still holds.
nodes.section: Solution of output feedback synchronized regulator problem

nodes.name: Jacobians of the augmented maps
nodes.statement: The Jacobian matrices of $\tilde{f}_i(\tilde{x}_i)$ and $\tilde{g}_i(\tilde{x}_i)$ have the form of \begin{equation} \tilde{A}_i=\left[ \frac{\partial \tilde{f}_i}{\partial \tilde{x}_i} \right]_{\tilde{x}_i=0}=\begin{bmatrix} A_i & 0 \\ -L_iC_i & A_i+L_iC_i \end{bmatrix}, \quad \tilde{B}_i=\left[ \frac{\partial \tilde{g}_i}{\partial \tilde{x}_i} \right]_{\tilde{x}_i=0}=\begin{bmatrix} B_i & 0 \\ 0 & B_i \end{bmatrix} \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Compute the linearization $(\tilde{A}_i,\tilde{B}_i)$ of the augmented system.
nodes.section: Solution of output feedback synchronized regulator problem

nodes.name: Apply Lemma 3 to the augmented system
nodes.statement: Noting that $\tilde{A}_i+\tilde{B}_i[0, K_i]$ has exactly the form \eqref{III23} and that controller \eqref{III24a} can be rewritten as $u_i=c_i(w_i)+[0, K_i](\tilde{x}_i-\tilde{\pi}_i(w_i))$, by Lemma \ref{le03} conditions 1a) and 1b) are satisfied for multi-agent system \eqref{III26} with controller \eqref{III24a}, and subsequently conditions 2a) and 2b) are satisfied for the closed-loop system \eqref{II07}. Therefore the output feedback synchronized regulator problem is solved under controller \eqref{III24}.
nodes.statement_short: Recognize the augmented closed loop as an instance of Lemma 3, giving conditions 2a) and 2b).
nodes.section: Solution of output feedback synchronized regulator problem
